The page names no date for any member's accession, so the shape is the adjusted -366 shape (104 cells, about 26,300 km2) plus Euboea (the Epaminondas page: 'The Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes'), 119 cells, about 30,100 km2 in all. The page gives no area; the prospectus of 377 and 'over 60 states' are all it says of extent.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 35,040 km2 (101 cells, Attica, the Aegean islands, Thracian coast and Corfu); the corrected shape is 104 cells, about 26,300 km2. Cliopatria puts Byzantium in the Theban row; the Epaminondas page says the 364 fleet 'achieved no lasting gains', and the Social War page has Byzantion revolting from Athens in 357, so it belongs here. Euboea is out from -370 (it defected to Thebes). Not verified within the page budget: the Thracian and Chalcidian cells (Abdera, Cardia, Torone, Amphipolis - the Macedonian dossier has Amphipolis taken by Philip in 357) and Corfu, which the page does not mention.

correction.text: the adjusted -366 shape with the Chersonese back ('finally ceded to the Athenians in 357 BC'); the four rebel cities are contested, not lost, until 355

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 11,560 km2 (34 cells, Attica, Lesbos, Samos, the Cyclades, Eretria); corrected 38 cells, about 9,600 km2: the Cersobleptes page has the Chersonese ceded in 357 and occupied 'with their settlers until 353 BC', and the Chaeronea page has Athens keeping Samos and Chalcis on its side in 338. Holds -350..-339; the league is dissolved in 338. Page silent on Mytilene, the Cyclades and Eretria after 355 (unverified: page budget).

region.text: meetings would be held in Athens

ledger.note: 378: Athens founds the Second Athenian League. The league 'existed from 378 to 355 BC' under the hegemony of Athens; its terms are the 'Decree of Aristoteles' (the page: '...signed the Decree of Aristoteles, which outlined the terms of the Second Athenian League'), and 'An inscribed prospectus for the League was found at Athens dating to 377 BC'. Thebes 'joined the league at its founding' and, after Leuctra (371), 'seceded from the League'; it is not drawn as league land. The year 378 is the page's; the region is the researcher's reading (Athens's own land).

region.text: Chios, Byzantium, Rhodes, and Mytilene ... among which were Kos, Mytilene, Rhodes, and Byzantium

ledger.note: 377: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion are among the founding allies. Athens 'reached out to Aegean cities under harsh Spartan control including Chios, Byzantium, Rhodes, and Mytilene'; the league 'included over 60 states, among which were Kos, Mytilene, Rhodes, and Byzantium'. The page gives no accession date for any of them (page silent), so 377, the prospectus year, is a bridge; their status as allies drawn in the lighter tint is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes

ledger.note: 377: Euboea is a member of the league. The Epaminondas page has only a footnote, 'The Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes'; the Second Athenian League page is silent on Euboea, so the accession year is a bridge to the prospectus year.

region.text: most of the allied cities became independent following the Social War

ledger.counterpart: Allied cities that became independent in 355
ledger.note: 377: the league's other Aegean and Thracian members join. 'It included over 60 states'; the page names no member beyond Chios, Byzantium, Rhodes, Mytilene and Kos, so the region is Cliopatria's -366 shape minus Attica, Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantium and minus the -350 shape (the members that left in 355).

ledger.counterpart: Allied cities that stayed with Athens
ledger.note: 377: the members that Athens kept after 355 join. The page does not say which members stayed (page silent); the region is Cliopatria's -350 shape without Attica and Euboea, kept at confidence 1.

region.text: the Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes

ledger.note: 370: Euboea defects to Thebes. 'The Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes' - a footnote attached to the 'By late 370' sentence of the Epaminondas page, with no year of its own (page silent); the Theban dossier opens the matching vassal event at -370.

360: Cotys I's Odrysians take the Thracian Chersonese from Athens. The Cersobleptes page is silent on the capture ('Cersobleptes inherited a conflict with the Athenians' from Cotys I) and says the peninsula was 'finally ceded to the Athenians in 357 BC'; the date and the capture come from the Odrysian dossier (Cotys I page, not opened here), hence confidence 1.

region.text: The peninsula seems to have been finally ceded to the Athenians in 357 BC

ledger.note: 357: Cersobleptes cedes the Thracian Chersonese to Athens. 'The peninsula seems to have been finally ceded to the Athenians in 357 BC' - the page's hedge, hence confidence 2 - and the Athenians 'did not occupy it with their settlers until 353 BC'. The struggle for it was fought through Charidemus, with Cersobleptes 'a mere puppet of Charidemus'.

region.text: Chios, Rhodes, Kos, and Byzantion went to war against Athens

ledger.note: 357: the Social War opens at Chios. 'During midsummer of 357 BC' the Athenian fleet under Chabrias was defeated and he 'was killed in the attack on the island of Chios'; the four allies 'overthrew their democratic governments and broke away from the league'. The page gives no date for the revolt itself; the first dated campaign is Chios in 357.

region.text: recognizing the independence of the confederate allies

ledger.note: 355: Athens makes peace and accepts its allies' independence. 'In 355 BC, Athens, not in any shape for another war, complied and withdrew by recognizing the independence of the confederate allies.' Embata (356): Timotheus and Iphicrates 'refused to engage due to a blowing gale' and Chares lost many ships; Persia had asked Athens to leave Asia Minor and threatened war.

region.text: the independence of the confederate allies

ledger.note: 355: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion leave the league for good ('Confederate allies independent' in the infobox).

region.text: most of the allied cities became independent following the Social War

ledger.counterpart: Allied cities that became independent in 355
ledger.note: 355: the league ends in all but name. 'The alliance lasted until 355 BC, when most of the allied cities became independent following the Social War.' The page lists no city but the four; the rest of the region is Cliopatria's -366 shape minus its -350 shape.

region.text: the independence of the confederate allies

ledger.note: 355: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion return to the Greek aggregate as independent cities (mirror of the Greek-city-states gain at -355).

region.text: most of the allied cities became independent following the Social War

ledger.note: 355: the other members that left become independent cities of the Greek aggregate; the region is the researcher's reading of 'most of the allied cities'.

350: Euboea is again on Athens's side. Cliopatria's -350 shape includes Eretria and the Chaeronea page lists Chalcis among Athens's allies in 338 ('Athens; Thebes; Corinth; Megara; Achaea; Chalcis; Epidaurus; Akarnania; Troezen'); the pages say nothing of when Euboea returned (page silent), so 350 is a bridge to the Cliopatria shape.

region.text: Corinth and Chalcis both received Macedonian garrisons

ledger.note: 338: Chalcis takes a Macedonian garrison after Chaeronea. 'Corinth and Chalcis both received Macedonian garrisons.'

region.text: the Second Athenian League was dissolved

ledger.counterpart: Allied cities that stayed with Athens
ledger.note: 338: the league is dissolved. After Chaeronea 'the Second Athenian League was dissolved'; 'the Athenians were allowed to keep their colony on Samos'. The month is not given.

region.text: the Second Athenian League was dissolved; the Athenians were allowed to keep their colony on Samos

ledger.note: 338: Attica and the rump of the league pass to the Macedonian-led Greek states. Philip's terms are not given for Attica beyond Samos staying Athenian; the League of Corinth 'was formed in the latter half of 337 BC' and 'all states signed up to the league, with the exception of Sparta'. Mirror of the Greek-city-states gain of Attica at -338.

region.text: the Second Athenian League was dissolved

ledger.note: 338: Chaeronea ends the Second Athenian League. 'the Second Athenian League was dissolved' (Chaeronea page, August 338 battle). The Second Athenian League page itself dates the end to 355 ('The alliance lasted until 355 BC'), when the allies left; Athens ran the rump to 338.

wars.name: Social War (357-355 BC)
wars.outcome: The four allies broke away and Athens recognised their independence in 355; most of the allied cities left the league.
wars.note: Chios (357, Chabrias killed), Embata (356), then 355; In 356 the allies ravaged Lemnos and Imbros, 'Athenian-loyal islands', and besieged Samos, which was 'defended by cleruchs' (the page gives no year for the siege). The infobox lists Mausolus among the allied commanders.

wars.name: Struggle for the Thracian Chersonese
wars.outcome: Cersobleptes ceded the peninsula to Athens in 357; Athenian settlers arrived in 353.
wars.note: The Odrysian dossier dates the war 363-357 from the Cotys I page, which was not opened here.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea (338 BC)
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory; the Second Athenian League was dissolved and Athens kept Samos.
wars.note: Infobox: August 338 BC; the majority of the allied troops came from Athens and Thebes.

certainty.note: No page gives a border. Attica is the one firm core; the allied lands are alliances of about 60 cities, and the Thracian, Aegean and Euboean reaches are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Second Athenian League' (-366..-338: 35,040 km2 to -351, then 11,560 km2) is Athens plus its allied cities. The dossier is written as the Athenian state (Attica as the direct core, the allied cities as client tint) so that Attica is drawn; as an association it would not be territory. Changes against Cliopatria: the start moves from -366 to -378 (new keyframe); the Byzantium and Kos cells are added (Cliopatria puts Byzantium in the Theban row); the big shape shrinks at -355, the page's date, not -351/-350; the Thracian Chersonese is out 360-357 and in from 357. Disagreement between pages: the Second Athenian League page ends the league in 355 ('The alliance lasted until 355 BC'), the Chaeronea page has 'the Second Athenian League was dissolved' in 338; the dossier keeps Cliopatria's end (338) and treats 355-338 as Athens's rump. Greek-city-states /ledger/28 removes the league at -377, the dossier founds it at -378 (the page's year). Page budget (1-2) exceeded to five: the Chersonese and Euboea needed their own pages; unverified: page budget - the Thracian and Chalcidian cells of the -366 shape (Abdera, Cardia, Torone, Amphipolis), Corfu, Mytilene and the Cyclades after 355, and the date Euboea returned. The -360 Chersonese loss is confidence 1 (the Cotys I page was not opened). Counterparts needing a dossier: Athens as a state of its own (this dossier carries Attica only for 378-338), the four rebel cities (Chios, Rhodes, Kos, Byzantion) are in the greek-city-states aggregate. Gazetteer names used: all resolvable (places Hios, Kos, Istanbul; regions Attica, Euboea, Rhodes).
